context.text: Incumbent Lizzie Pannill Fletcher (D) ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary. Alexander Hale won a May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff against Tina Blum Cohen, 64.3% to 35.7%. As of September 2026, forecasters (Cook Political Report, Decision Desk HQ, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rated the general election Solid/Safe Democratic.

candidates.name: Lizzie Pannill Fletcher

summary.text: Lizzie Pannill Fletcher is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 7th Congressional District. A Houston native and former litigation lawyer, she was first elected in 2018 by defeating Republican incumbent John Culberson and now serves as Vice Ranking Member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

background.text: Born in Houston, Texas, and graduated from St. John's School. According to her official biography, she has been a resident of Houston and the 7th District nearly all of her life.
Graduated from Kenyon College in Ohio in 1997 with highest honors in History and was elected to Phi Beta Kappa.
After college, worked in the business and non-profit sectors for six years before attending William & Mary Law School, where she was editor-in-chief of the William and Mary Law Review.
Began her legal career at Vinson & Elkins in Houston and later joined the litigation firm AZA, where she became its first woman partner.
Co-founded Planned Parenthood Young Leaders in 2000 and has served on the boards of Writers in the Schools and the Open Dance Project.

Won the 2018 Democratic primary runoff over Laura Moser and then the November 2018 general election over incumbent Republican John Culberson; took office in January 2019 and has been re-elected since.

In the 119th Congress, serves as Vice Ranking Member of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, with subcommittee seats on Health, Energy, and Oversight and Investigations. Earlier terms included service on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

Chairs the Texas Democratic Delegation, serves on the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee, and is a Deputy Whip of the House Democratic Caucus; co-chairs the Flood Resilience Caucus and the Natural Gas Caucus and is a member of the New Democrat Coalition.
According to her official biography, she lives in Houston with her husband, Scott.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including the Health Subcommittee and the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee, in the 2025–2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Alexander Hale
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff against Tina Blum Cohen

summary.text: Alexander Hale is the Republican nominee for Texas's 7th Congressional District. A Houston native and Baylor University graduate, he works as an energy and chemicals consultant and, according to his campaign website, is running on Houston's energy economy, affordability, public safety, and fiscal responsibility.

background.text: According to his campaign website, a fourth-generation Houstonian who grew up in Houston.

Attended Baylor University on an academic scholarship, where he says he majored in Finance, Political Science, Philosophy, and Business Fellows and founded the university's Alexander Hamilton Society chapter.
During college summers, says he worked in Washington, D.C. for the American Enterprise Institute and for U.S. Senator Ben Sasse, and interned for Patriot Capital.
After graduating, returned to Houston to work in financial services and energy; his campaign website lists him as an Energy and Chemicals Consultant at Alvarez & Marsal.
Advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 45.3% of the vote and won the May 26, 2026 runoff over Tina Blum Cohen, 64.3% to 35.7%.
Describes himself as a devout Christian, says he lives in the Heights neighborhood of Houston, and says he serves at his church.

candidates.name: Espoir Ngabo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Green Party convention nomination

summary.text: Espoir Ngabo is an information-technology professional running as the Green Party nominee for Texas's 7th Congressional District. He advanced from the Green Party convention on March 21, 2026, and in his Ballotpedia survey says his campaign accepts no corporate money.

background.text: Describes a career of nearly a decade in information technology, supporting business systems and infrastructure.
Says he is based in Houston and connected to the Alief, Sharpstown, and Gulfton communities.
Advanced from the Green Party convention for the seat on March 21, 2026.

priorities.text: Says his campaign takes zero corporate money and is "powered by everyday people."
Calls for stronger flood protection and disaster preparedness, reliable public transit, and safer roads and sidewalks in the district.
